en.name: Titus Brandsma
en.summary: Dutch Carmelite priest and journalism professor murdered at Dachau after publicly instructing Catholic newspapers to refuse Nazi propaganda.
en.body: Titus Brandsma was a Dutch Carmelite priest, philosophy professor, and rector of the Catholic University of Nijmegen who also worked extensively as a journalist and spiritual advisor to the Dutch Catholic press. When Nazi occupation authorities in the Netherlands ordered newspapers to publish party propaganda and advertisements, Brandsma, acting on behalf of the Dutch bishops, personally traveled to editors across the country instructing them to refuse the order regardless of the consequences, an act of direct defiance that led to his arrest by the Gestapo in 1942. He was held in several prisons and eventually transported to Dachau concentration camp, where, weakened by torture and starvation, he continued quietly ministering to fellow prisoners until he was killed by lethal injection in the camp's infirmary. He was canonized by Pope Francis in 2022 and is honored as a patron of journalists and defenders of a free press.
